column3: CO-1: Customer Shopping Cart
column11: Enable customers to add, update, and remove products from a shopping cart before placing an order.

column3: CO-2: Order Review & Checkout
column11: Provide a checkout experience allowing customers to review their order, enter shipping information, and confirm their purchase.

column3: CO-3: Payment Processing
column11: Securely process customer payments using supported payment methods and validate successful authorization before order submission.

column3: CO-4: Order Confirmation & Notifications
column11: Generate an order confirmation and notify customers through email or SMS after a successful purchase.

column3: CO-5: Order Status & Tracking
column11: Allow customers to view current order status, shipment progress, and estimated delivery information.

column3: CO-6: Order History
column11: Provide customers with access to previous orders, order details, and the ability to reorder previously purchased items.

column3: FR-1 - The system shall allow authenticated customers to update their mailing address through the customer portal.
column11: Business capability: Enable authenticated customers to update their mailing address through the existing self-service portal. Customer value: Customers can maintain accurate address information without contacting Customer Support, improving convenience and reducing support workload. Expected outcome: A submitted mailing-address change is validated, processed, reflected in the customer profile, recorded in the audit history, and made visible through request status. Assumptions: The customer is authenticated; an existing customer profile is available; the customer portal, Customer Profile Service, and Address Validation Service are available. Architecture considerations: Reuse the existing portal, Identity Provider, API Gateway, Customer Profile Service, Profile Data Store, Address Validation Service, audit logging, and cloud platform. Protect PII, enforce identity and tenant authorization, validate and normalize addresses, preserve existing profile-viewing functionality, meet performance and availability objectives, and support reliable processing across multiple availability zones.

column3: FR-10 - The system shall return processing status to the customer.
column11: Business capability: Provide customer-visible status for an accepted profile-update request. Customer value: Customers understand whether their request is processing, completed, or failed without contacting Customer Support. Expected outcome: The portal uses the request identifier to retrieve and display a current, tenant-scoped processing status and final outcome. Assumptions: Accepted requests are assigned a durable request identifier and the Customer Profile Service can maintain request state. Architecture considerations: Reuse the portal, API Gateway, and profile service status capability; enforce authorization and tenant isolation; meet response-time and availability targets; protect PII; retain failed requests for investigation; and ensure status remains accurate during retries, recovery, and staged rollout.

column3: FR-11 - The system shall record all profile changes in an audit log.
column11: Business capability: Maintain a complete audit history for accepted customer profile changes. Customer value: Supports trust, issue investigation, compliance, and accountability for changes to sensitive profile information. Expected outcome: Each accepted update records the actor, timestamp, tenant, request identifier, changed fields, prior values, new values, and result in a tamper-resistant audit record. Assumptions: An approved audit logging capability exists and retention and support-search requirements will be resolved. Architecture considerations: Protect PII, encrypt audit data, enforce tenant-scoped access, maintain tamper resistance, keep audit and profile-update outcomes consistent, support required retention policies, avoid exposing sensitive values in operational logs, and provide sufficient reliability so no completed change lacks an audit record.

column3: FR-12 - The system shall notify the customer when processing completes successfully.
column11: Business capability: Notify the customer after a profile-update request completes successfully. Customer value: Provides confirmation that requested changes were completed and reduces uncertainty or repeat submissions. Expected outcome: A profile-update confirmation is sent through the existing Email Notification Service after successful processing. Assumptions: The notification service is available; a profile-update template and event or request type can be created; confirmation emails are required unless the open product decision changes. Architecture considerations: Reuse the existing notification integration, protect PII, use the customer's confirmed email address, propagate correlation information, monitor notification failures, scale with request volume, and define whether notification delivery failure changes the customer-visible completion status.

column3: FR-13 - The system shall return meaningful error messages when processing cannot be completed with contact information to report the problem.
column11: Business capability: Provide meaningful customer-facing errors and support contact information when a profile-update request cannot be completed. Customer value: Customers understand that the request failed, know what action to take, and can obtain assistance without ambiguity. Expected outcome: Failed requests reach a visible terminal status with an actionable message, a support path, and an operationally useful error reference while retained for investigation. Assumptions: Operational error categories and approved Customer Support contact information are available. Architecture considerations: Translate internal failures into safe customer messages, avoid exposing PII or implementation details, retain correlation identifiers and failed-request state, enforce tenant-scoped status access, monitor and alert on sustained failures, support recovery procedures, and meet accessibility, reliability, and privacy standards.

column3: FR-2 - The system shall allow authenticated customers to update their email address through the customer portal.
column11: Business capability: Enable authenticated customers to update their email address through the existing self-service portal. Customer value: Customers can maintain accurate contact information without Customer Support intervention and receive communications at the correct address. Expected outcome: A valid email-address change is securely processed, reflected in the customer profile, recorded in the audit history, and available through request status. Assumptions: The customer is authenticated; an existing customer profile is available; existing customer data services support profile updates. Architecture considerations: Reuse the existing portal, Identity Provider, API Gateway, Customer Profile Service, Profile Data Store, audit logging, and cloud platform. Protect PII, enforce tenant isolation and authorization, apply required-field and format validation, consider whether ownership verification or step-up authentication is required, and meet reliability, performance, availability, and privacy requirements.

column3: FR-3- The system shall allow authenticated customers to update their phone number through the customer portal.
column11: Business capability: Enable authenticated customers to update their phone number through the existing self-service portal. Customer value: Customers can maintain accurate contact information without Customer Support intervention. Expected outcome: A valid phone-number change is securely processed, reflected in the customer profile, recorded in the audit history, and available through request status. Assumptions: The customer is authenticated; an existing customer profile is available; existing customer data services support profile updates. Architecture considerations: Reuse the existing portal, Identity Provider, API Gateway, Customer Profile Service, Profile Data Store, audit logging, and cloud platform. Protect PII, enforce tenant isolation and authorization, apply required-field and format validation, consider whether ownership verification or step-up authentication is required, and meet reliability, performance, availability, and privacy requirements.

column3: FR-4 - The system shall allow authenticated customers to update a combination of mailing address, email address and phone number in a single submission.
column11: Business capability: Allow an authenticated customer to submit changes to one or more supported profile fields in a single request. Customer value: Customers can complete profile maintenance efficiently without making separate submissions for each field. Expected outcome: The combined request is validated as a unit, processed reliably, reflected consistently in the customer profile, recorded in the audit history, and tracked through a single request status. Assumptions: Individual mailing-address, email-address, and phone-number updates are supported; the existing profile service can process multi-field changes consistently. Architecture considerations: Coordinate validation for each changed field, invoke address validation only when applicable, preserve data consistency during partial or concurrent updates, use tenant-scoped records and concurrency controls, protect PII, and ensure audit and status information identifies all changed fields.

column3: FR-5 - The system shall validate all required fields before accepting a request.
column11: Business capability: Validate required profile fields before a customer update request is accepted for processing. Customer value: Customers receive immediate feedback and avoid submitting incomplete requests that would fail later. Expected outcome: Incomplete or invalid submissions are rejected without changing stored profile data, while valid submissions can proceed to processing. Assumptions: Required fields and validation rules are defined for mailing address, email address, and phone number. Architecture considerations: Apply consistent validation across the portal and Customer Profile Service, with the service remaining authoritative. Protect PII in validation responses and telemetry, maintain two-second response objectives under normal conditions, support horizontal scaling, and ensure validation behavior is tenant-aware and does not affect existing profile viewing.

column3: FR-6 - The system shall validate the submitted address using an external address validation service.
column11: Business capability: Validate and normalize submitted mailing addresses using the external Address Validation Service before accepting an address update. Customer value: Improves profile-data accuracy and reduces failed communications or downstream correction work. Expected outcome: Address submissions receive a valid normalized result, a candidate correction, or a clear validation failure before processing continues. Assumptions: An approved provider, interface, credentials, rate limits, timeout behavior, and test environment are available. Architecture considerations: Use a secure service-side integration over TLS, apply explicit timeouts and appropriate failure handling, protect PII, prevent provider latency from exhausting resources, support scaling for concurrent requests, and define behavior when the provider is unavailable or an address cannot be verified.

column3: FR-7 - The system shall display validation errors to the customer with instructions on how to resolve
column11: Business capability: Present actionable validation errors when submitted profile information cannot be accepted. Customer value: Customers can understand and correct problems without contacting Customer Support. Expected outcome: The portal identifies the affected field, explains the issue in meaningful language, and provides guidance for correction without exposing sensitive technical information. Assumptions: Validation services return usable error categories or codes that can be translated into customer-facing guidance. Architecture considerations: Coordinate portal and service validation responses, support address-correction candidates where applicable, meet accessibility requirements, avoid exposing PII or internal system details, preserve correlation information for support, and maintain responsive behavior under normal operating conditions.

column3: FR-8 - The system shall submit valid requests to an automated workflow for processing.
column11: Business capability: Accept a valid profile-update request and submit it to an automated workflow for reliable processing. Customer value: Profile changes can be completed quickly and consistently without manual Customer Support activity. Expected outcome: Each accepted request receives a request identifier, is durably recorded, enters Processing status, and proceeds to a safe terminal outcome without being lost. Assumptions: The existing Customer Profile Service can be extended to support orchestration and durable request status, or an architecture decision will identify an alternative. Architecture considerations: Reuse the API Gateway and Customer Profile Service where practical; support asynchronous processing, idempotency, bounded retry, correlation identifiers, tenant isolation, horizontal scaling, multi-availability-zone deployment, observability, and recovery of failed requests.

column3: FR-9 - The system shall update the customer profile after successful processing.
column11: Business capability: Persist successfully processed mailing-address, email-address, and phone-number changes to the customer profile. Customer value: Customers see accurate current profile information after a completed request. Expected outcome: Authorized changes are stored consistently, do not overwrite newer updates, and become available through existing profile-viewing functionality. Assumptions: The Customer Profile Service and Profile Data Store support updates and appropriate concurrency controls; authoritative ownership of each profile field is confirmed. Architecture considerations: Enforce identity and tenant authorization, protect PII in transit and at rest, use concurrency controls to prevent lost updates, maintain consistency with audit and status outcomes, support reliable recovery from partial failure, and avoid degrading existing profile APIs.
